brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base holding removable bins for small parts (at least 2 bins).
requirements.evidence: Two bins sit in the base: hex-bin-full-div2 at (0,0,0) and hex-bin-full at (0,1,0), both with role R1. check_build shows meshClash clear, with no rule errors. Removability is the bin's drop-in design; I did not test removing them.

The only drawer-type part is a notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, family notch) at (-1,1,0). It is not a family 'drawer' part. Real drawer offers on a half base's cut face never appeared: the half base at (1,0,0) gave none, with or without its top cover and bolts, and removing the neighbour at (2,0,0) did not open one. The test for family 'drawer' will fail.

A handle (handle:1,1,0;top) with inserts was added at (1,1,0) when the covers (1,0), (1,1), (2,0) formed its triangle. I then removed the piece, cover and joint bolt at (2,0) for a drawer test that failed. That breaks the triangle the handle requires, so the handle is no longer supported by a closed triangle. check_build is still clear, but I did not re-verify the handle after the removal. Restoring the (2,0) piece, its top cover and the joint bolt at (1,1) slot 1 would likely fix it.

finish.summary: The build is a small base: a full cell at (0,0) with a div2 bin, a full cell at (0,1) with a full bin, a half-east cell at (1,0) with a top cover, and a notch drawer frame at (-1,1). A carry handle sat on a triangle of covers at (1,0), (1,1) and (2,0), with joint bolts. check_build is clear (meshClash clear, no rule errors) except a LOOSE_BODY warning on the half cell at (1,0). Two problems remain. First, no real 'drawer' part ever became available: the notch frame is the only drawer-type offer, so R2 is unmet by the family test. Second, my late test removed the (2,0) piece, which broke the handle's triangle, so R3 is only partial and needs that piece, its cover and a bolt restored. I ran out of turns before I could repair it.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
